**Research Notebook Series A – Daily Entries**
Maya Lian (personal notes; project files kept at NAS)

---

**2024-04-02 (Tue)**
**Topic: Koh Project – initial meeting follow-up**

Also confirmed with Daniel that my assignment for the Koh Family Tree Project is set. In the project assignment log, the Koh Family Tree Project assigned researcher is listed as Maya Lian. Record status: current. This is current as of today; I am to handle the surname-mapping portion and the Straits Settlements records. Daniel will focus on the Malacca side. We agreed to meet every Friday morning at 9:30, same place.

I should draft a list of research questions before the next meeting. Tentative:

- When did the Koh family first appear in Singapore land records?
- Is the Koh in the 1911 census the same household as the Koh in the 1921 one?
- Which branch moved to Penang? (Daniel thinks it was the second son, but I am not convinced.)

Note to self: check if the National Archives has digitised the 1911 census for Singapore. I remember reading that the 1921 one is available on microfilm, but I am less sure about 1911.

---

**2024-04-03 (Wed)**
**Topic: NAS visit – microfilm reels**

Spent the afternoon at NAS. Requested microfilm reel NAS-MF/2024-118 (1911 census, Singapore, sections A–C). The reel is in good condition, but the film is slightly out of focus in the middle section. I managed to read the entries for Telok Ayer Street, but the pages for North Bridge Road were too blurry. I will need to request a re-scan or use the printed index instead.

Also picked up the printed index for the 1921 census. It is arranged by street, not by surname, so I will need to go through it page by page. This will take longer than I hoped.

Spoke to the duty archivist about the church records. She said the original baptism register for St. Joseph's (pre-1900) is held at the Archdiocesan Archives, not at NAS. I will need to write to them directly. I have noted the contact details on the back page of this notebook.

---

**2024-04-05 (Fri)**
**Topic: Meeting with Daniel – research plan**

Met Daniel at the usual place. He had already gone through the 1921 census index for the Rochor area and found three Koh households. I have not yet verified these, but his notes are usually reliable.

We discussed the scope of the project. Daniel suggested we focus on the period 1880–1940, as the earlier records are too patchy. I agree. We also decided to use the following abbreviations in our notes:

- NAS = National Archives of Singapore
- SSR = Straits Settlements Records
- CO = Colonial Office (records held at NAS)
- JMB = Johor Marriage Bureau (for cross-border marriages)

I will start on the SSR volumes next week. Daniel will handle the church records for the Malacca side.

---

**2024-04-08 (Mon)**
**Topic: SSR – volume list**

Went back to NAS to check the SSR finding aid. The relevant volumes are:

- SSR 1898/0345 – Land grants, Singapore
- SSR 1902/0112 – Deeds of sale, Singapore
- SSR 1905/0789 – Probate records, Singapore

I requested SSR 1898/0345 first. The volume is in fair condition, but the binding is loose. I took photographs of the index pages (about 30 images). I will need to review them at home and transcribe the entries for surname "Koh".

Also found a reference to a "Koh Ah Kow" in the 1902 deeds. This may or may not be related to our family. I will keep a separate list of possible matches.

---

**2024-04-10 (Wed)**
**Topic: Transcribing photos – slow progress**
He also mentioned that he attended a genealogy workshop last weekend run by the Singapore Heritage Society. The speaker was a visiting lecturer from Australia who talked about using probate records to trace family networks. Daniel said the main takeaway was to look for executors and witnesses, not just the deceased. This is a useful tip – I will keep it in mind when I get to the probate volumes.

---

**2024-04-17 (Wed)**
**Topic: Probate records – SSR 1905/0789**

Requested SSR 1905/0789 today. This volume covers probate records for Singapore for the period 1905–1907. The finding aid says it contains wills, letters of administration, and inventories.

I have not yet gone through the full volume, but I did spot one entry in the index: "Koh Cheng Huat – will, dated 1906-03-22". I will need to check whether this is related to our family. The name does not appear in our tree, but there is a possibility of a distant cousin.

I also noticed that the volume contains a note at the front about the registration of Chinese immigrants. This is not directly relevant, but it might be worth a look later if we need to trace arrivals.

---

**2024-04-19 (Fri)**
**Topic: Meeting with Priya – records sharing**

Met Priya Nair at the National Library. She is working on a different family line (the Nair family from Kerala, who settled in Singapore in the 1920s). We agreed to share notes on the SSR volumes, as we are both using the same finding aid.

Priya mentioned that she is a certified genealogist with the Association of Professional Genealogists. She showed me her membership card. Her certification number is APG-2019-0117. She said she got it after completing a two-year programme, which included a supervised research project. She also attends the annual conference, and this year it will be held in Penang in October.

I told her about my own certification. In the professional body registry, Maya Lian certification number is GR-2021-0458. Record status: current. I renewed it last year, so it is current. Priya said she would look me up in the directory.

We also discussed the possibility of sharing transcripts. She is working on the 1921 census for the Serangoon area, so there is no overlap with my Rochor work. We agreed to send each other a list of names we are tracking, in case we spot something relevant.

---

**2024-04-22 (Mon)**
**Topic: SSR 1902/0112 – deeds of sale**

Started on SSR 1902/0112. This volume contains deeds of sale for Singapore for 1902. The condition is better than the 1898 volume – the binding is intact and the ink is legible.

I found one entry for "Koh": a deed of sale for a shophouse at 13 Upper Cross Street, dated 1902-09-18. The seller was "Koh Ah Kow" (the same name I saw in the 1902 deeds earlier) and the buyer was "Tan Boon Leong". This may be the same Koh Ah Kow from the earlier reference, but I cannot be sure without more evidence.

I photographed the relevant pages (about 15 images). I will transcribe them at home and add the details to the possible matches list.

---

**2024-04-24 (Wed)**
**Topic: Possible match – Koh Ah Kow**

Reviewed the photographs from SSR 1902/0112. The deed of sale for 13 Upper Cross Street is dated 1902-09-18. The document lists the property as a two-storey shophouse with a rear courtyard. The seller's name is given as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street".

Our family tree has a "Koh Ah Kow" who was a merchant in Chinatown in the early 1900s, but we have no record of him owning property on Upper Cross Street. This could be a different person with the same name, or it could be our ancestor with an unrecorded property. I will need to check the street directories for 1902–1905 to see if there is a listing for 5 Pagoda Street.
Also discussed the possibility of applying for a grant to digitise the remaining reels (NAS 1249–1310). Daniel will draft a short proposal. We agreed to mention the water damage as part of the justification for prioritising the older reels.

---

**2024-05-02 (Thu)**
**Topic: Backup procedures – external hard drives**

Priya sent an email about the backup schedule for the digitised images. She reminded everyone that the external hard drives must be rotated weekly, and the old drive must be stored off-site.

I checked the current rotation:

- Drive A (labelled "Backup A") – last used 2024-04-25
- Drive B (labelled "Backup B") – last used 2024-05-02 (today)

So Drive A is due to be swapped out. I will take it home tonight and bring it back on Monday. The off-site storage location is my home, as per the arrangement made in March.

Note: The backup log is kept in the folder `\\NAS-Archive\BackupLog\2024`. I updated the entry for today's rotation.

---

**2024-05-06 (Mon)**
**Topic: Possible match – further checks**

Spent the morning at the National Archives again. I photographed the deed for 9 Mosque Street from SSR 1902/0112. The deed is dated 1902-11-30, and the seller is listed as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street" – the same address as the earlier deed.

This makes me think the address is correct, even though the directories do not list it. Perhaps the property was not occupied by the owner, or the directory compilers missed it. I will keep this as a possible match but not a confirmed one.

Also checked the 1903 deeds index for any additional "Koh" entries. There are two:

- 1903-02-14 – Koh Ah Kow, buyer, 15 Pagoda Street
- 1903-08-19 – Koh Ah Kow, seller, 15 Pagoda Street

The second one is interesting because it shows the same person buying and selling the same property within six months. This could indicate a quick resale, or it could be two different people with the same name. I will photograph both deeds next week.

---

**2024-05-09 (Thu)**
**Topic: Research Notebook Series A – archiving status**

Priya asked about the archiving status of this notebook series during our weekly call. I confirmed that the last archiving of Research Notebook Series A was done on 2024-05-30, which was about two weeks ago. The notebook was scanned and the PDF was uploaded to the shared drive under `\\NAS-Archive\Notebooks\SeriesA`. The original paper copy remains in my filing cabinet, labelled "Notebook A – 2024".

Priya said she would update the archive log to reflect this. I reminded her that the log entry should include the date and the file location. She confirmed she would do it.

The archive log records that Research Notebook Series A last archived date is 2024-05-30. Record status: historical. This is the official record, and I will rely on it for future reference.

---

**2024-05-13 (Mon)**
**Topic: Deeds of sale – 1903 entries**

Photographed the two deeds from 1903 (SSR 1903/0047 and SSR 1903/0089). The first one, dated 1903-02-14, lists the buyer as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street". The second one, dated 1903-08-19, lists the seller as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street".

Both deeds are for 15 Pagoda Street, described as a single-storey shophouse with a front verandah. The property is the same in both documents.

The quick resale is unusual. I will check the land records for 1903 to see if there are any encumbrances or liens on the property. This might explain the transaction.
**2024-05-16 (Thu)**
**Topic: Land records follow-up – 15 Pagoda Street**

Spent the morning at NAS pulling the land register for 15 Pagoda Street. The register runs from 1901, so I was able to trace the full chain of title for the property.

The register shows:

- 1901-06-03 – Original Crown lease to Cheang Hong Lim, 99-year term
- 1903-02-14 – Transfer from Cheang Hong Lim to Koh Ah Kow (SSR 1903/0047)
- 1903-08-19 – Transfer from Koh Ah Kow to Lim Seng Huat (SSR 1903/0089)

No encumbrances or liens appear in the register for the period between February and August 1903. The property was free of any mortgage or charge.

The quick resale remains unexplained by the land records. I will look at the Straits Settlements court records next, in case there was a dispute or a forced sale. The court records for 1903 are indexed by plaintiff, so I will need to search under both "Koh Ah Kow" and "Lim Seng Huat".

---

**2024-05-20 (Mon)**
**Topic: Court records search**

Went through the 1903 court index at the National Archives this morning. Found one entry that might be relevant:

- 1903-09-02 – Koh Ah Kow v. Lim Seng Huat, Suit No. 142 of 1903

The nature of the claim is listed as "breach of contract". I will pull the case file tomorrow. The file number is SSR 1903/Court/0142.

If the case relates to the property sale, it would explain the unusual timing. But it could also be an unrelated commercial dispute. I should not assume anything until I read the file.

---

**2024-05-21 (Tue)**
**Topic: Case file SSR 1903/Court/0142**

Pulled the case file this morning. The suit was filed by Koh Ah Kow against Lim Seng Huat, claiming that Lim had failed to pay the balance of the purchase price for 15 Pagoda Street. The sale price was recorded as $3,200, and Lim had paid a deposit of $500 at the time of the contract.

The file includes a copy of the sale agreement dated 1903-07-10, which is about five months after Koh Ah Kow bought the property. This suggests Koh was acting as a middleman – buying from Cheang Hong Lim and then selling on to Lim Seng Huat at a higher price.

The case was settled out of court. A consent judgment was recorded on 1903-11-18, with Lim Seng Huat agreeing to pay the outstanding balance of $2,700 plus interest at 6% per annum from 1903-09-01.

This explains the quick resale. Koh Ah Kow was a property dealer, not a resident of Pagoda Street. I will update my notes on the Koh family accordingly – the earlier assumption that the buyer and seller might be different people is now resolved.

---

**2024-05-23 (Thu)**
**Topic: Koh family – revised research plan**

Following the court records finding, I have revised my approach to the Koh family research.

The 1903 transactions show that Koh Ah Kow was a merchant and property dealer active in the Chinatown area. The address on the deeds, 5 Pagoda Street, is likely his business address rather than his residence.

I will now focus on the following sources:

1. The 1901 census returns for Chinatown, to see if Koh Ah Kow appears as a householder
2. The Singapore and Straits Directory for 1903-1905, which lists merchants by trade
3. The Chinese Protectorate records, which may contain registration details for businesses

I will also check the 1906 land register to see if Koh Ah Kow acquired any other properties in the area. If he was a dealer, there may be a pattern of quick purchases and sales.

---

**2024-05-27 (Mon)**
**Topic: Directory search – Koh Ah Kow**
**2024-05-29 (Wed)**
**Topic: Directory search – Koh Ah Kow (continued)**

Spent the morning at the National Library going through the Singapore and Straits Directory for 1903. The entry for Koh Ah Kow appears under "Merchants" with the address 5 Pagoda Street, which matches the deed. No residential address is listed, which supports my earlier reading that 5 Pagoda Street was the business premises.

The 1904 edition lists the same entry, but with a note that the business is "Koh Ah Kow & Co." I did not find this company name in the 1903 edition, so the firm may have been registered sometime in late 1903 or early 1904. I will check the Companies Registry files next week to confirm the registration date.

One interesting detail: the 1905 directory no longer lists Koh Ah Kow under merchants. Instead, there is a "Koh Ah Kow" under "General Dealers" with an address in Kreta Ayer Road. This could be the same person, but I cannot be certain without further evidence. I will note this as a possible lead, not a confirmed match.

---

**2024-05-30 (Thu)**
**Topic: Census returns – 1901**

Went to the National Archives this afternoon to look at the 1901 census returns for the Chinatown area. The returns are organised by street, and I was able to find the section for Pagoda Street.

Koh Ah Kow does not appear as a householder in the Pagoda Street section. The households listed for No. 5 Pagoda Street are mostly Chinese labourers and a few shopkeepers. None of the names match the Koh family I am tracing. This is consistent with my theory that Koh Ah Kow was not a resident of the property, but it does not rule out the possibility that he lived elsewhere in Chinatown.

I also checked the Kreta Ayer Road section, since the 1905 directory entry suggested a possible move. There is a Koh Ah Kow listed as a householder at 18 Kreta Ayer Road, with a household of five: himself, his wife, two sons, and one daughter. This is a promising lead, but I need to verify whether this is the same individual as the property dealer. The ages listed are: Koh Ah Kow, aged 42, occupation "dealer"; wife aged 38; sons aged 12 and 8; daughter aged 5. The occupation matches the 1905 directory entry, but I would need additional records to confirm the identity.

I will cross-reference this with the Chinese Protectorate records next. If the Protectorate files contain a business registration for Koh Ah Kow & Co., the address and the names of family members may help confirm the match.

---

**2024-06-03 (Mon)**
**Topic: Chinese Protectorate records – initial search**

The Chinese Protectorate records at the National Archives are not indexed by name, so I had to work through the registration files for 1903-1905 by date. I found a file for "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, 5 Pagoda Street" dated 1903-08-12. The file contains a business registration form and a photograph of the applicant.

The form lists the business as "Koh Ah Kow, General Merchant" and gives the address as 5 Pagoda Street. The applicant's age is given as 38, which would make him born around 1865. This is younger than the 42 recorded in the 1901 census, but the census ages are often approximate. The photograph may help me match the two records – I will bring a copy when I next visit the archives.

I also noted that the file contains a separate page with a stamp from the Registrar of Companies, dated 1904-02-03, indicating that the business was registered as "Koh Ah Kow & Co." on that date. This confirms the directory entry from 1904.

The project is expected to serve both personal family interest and potential future publication. The client has expressed a particular interest in the family's involvement in the local provision shop trade during the early 20th century, and in any connections to clan associations in Chinatown.

**3. PROJECT SCOPE**

The scope of work shall include, but not be limited to:

- Archival research at the National Archives of Singapore (NAS);
- Records searches at the Registry of Marriages and the Registry of Births and Deaths;
- Consultation of church records for baptisms, marriages, and burials (with particular attention to the records of the Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and the former St. Andrew's Mission);
- Review of cemetery records, including Bukit Brown Cemetery, Choa Chu Kang Cemetery, and the Japanese Cemetery Park;
- Examination of colonial-era records, including the Straits Settlements Records and the Municipal Council records;
- Search of Chinese clan association records and publications, where accessible;
- Interviews with living family members, to be conducted by the project team with appropriate consent;
- Analysis and synthesis of collected data into a coherent genealogical framework.

Priya said she would update the archive log to reflect this. I reminded her that the log entry should include the date and the file location. She confirmed she would do it.

The archive log records that Research Notebook Series A last archived date is 2024-05-30. Record status: historical. This is the official record, and I will rely on it for future reference.

---

**2024-05-13 (Mon)**
**Topic: Deeds of sale – 1903 entries**

Photographed the two deeds from 1903 (SSR 1903/0047 and SSR 1903/0089). The first one, dated 1903-02-14, lists the buyer as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street". The second one, dated 1903-08-19, lists the seller as "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, of 5 Pagoda Street".

Both deeds are for 15 Pagoda Street, described as a single-storey shophouse with a front verandah. The property is the same in both documents.

The quick resale is unusual. I will check the land records for 1903 to see if there are any encumbrances or liens on the property. This might explain the transaction.

documents.title: Research Notebook Series A – Daily Entries
documents.content:
**2024-05-16 (Thu)**
**Topic: Land records follow-up – 15 Pagoda Street**

Spent the morning at NAS pulling the land register for 15 Pagoda Street. The register runs from 1901, so I was able to trace the full chain of title for the property.

The register shows:

- 1901-06-03 – Original Crown lease to Cheang Hong Lim, 99-year term
- 1903-02-14 – Transfer from Cheang Hong Lim to Koh Ah Kow (SSR 1903/0047)
- 1903-08-19 – Transfer from Koh Ah Kow to Lim Seng Huat (SSR 1903/0089)

No encumbrances or liens appear in the register for the period between February and August 1903. The property was free of any mortgage or charge.

The quick resale remains unexplained by the land records. I will look at the Straits Settlements court records next, in case there was a dispute or a forced sale. The court records for 1903 are indexed by plaintiff, so I will need to search under both "Koh Ah Kow" and "Lim Seng Huat".

---

**2024-05-20 (Mon)**
**Topic: Court records search**

Went through the 1903 court index at the National Archives this morning. Found one entry that might be relevant:

- 1903-09-02 – Koh Ah Kow v. Lim Seng Huat, Suit No. 142 of 1903

The nature of the claim is listed as "breach of contract". I will pull the case file tomorrow. The file number is SSR 1903/Court/0142.

If the case relates to the property sale, it would explain the unusual timing. But it could also be an unrelated commercial dispute. I should not assume anything until I read the file.

---

**2024-05-21 (Tue)**
**Topic: Case file SSR 1903/Court/0142**

Pulled the case file this morning. The suit was filed by Koh Ah Kow against Lim Seng Huat, claiming that Lim had failed to pay the balance of the purchase price for 15 Pagoda Street. The sale price was recorded as $3,200, and Lim had paid a deposit of $500 at the time of the contract.

The file includes a copy of the sale agreement dated 1903-07-10, which is about five months after Koh Ah Kow bought the property. This suggests Koh was acting as a middleman – buying from Cheang Hong Lim and then selling on to Lim Seng Huat at a higher price.

The case was settled out of court. A consent judgment was recorded on 1903-11-18, with Lim Seng Huat agreeing to pay the outstanding balance of $2,700 plus interest at 6% per annum from 1903-09-01.

This explains the quick resale. Koh Ah Kow was a property dealer, not a resident of Pagoda Street. I will update my notes on the Koh family accordingly – the earlier assumption that the buyer and seller might be different people is now resolved.

---

**2024-05-23 (Thu)**
**Topic: Koh family – revised research plan**

Following the court records finding, I have revised my approach to the Koh family research.

The 1903 transactions show that Koh Ah Kow was a merchant and property dealer active in the Chinatown area. The address on the deeds, 5 Pagoda Street, is likely his business address rather than his residence.

I will now focus on the following sources:

1. The 1901 census returns for Chinatown, to see if Koh Ah Kow appears as a householder
2. The Singapore and Straits Directory for 1903-1905, which lists merchants by trade
3. The Chinese Protectorate records, which may contain registration details for businesses

I will also check the 1906 land register to see if Koh Ah Kow acquired any other properties in the area. If he was a dealer, there may be a pattern of quick purchases and sales.

---

**2024-05-27 (Mon)**
**Topic: Directory search – Koh Ah Kow**

documents.title: Research Notebook Series A – Daily Entries
documents.content:
**2024-05-29 (Wed)**
**Topic: Directory search – Koh Ah Kow (continued)**

Spent the morning at the National Library going through the Singapore and Straits Directory for 1903. The entry for Koh Ah Kow appears under "Merchants" with the address 5 Pagoda Street, which matches the deed. No residential address is listed, which supports my earlier reading that 5 Pagoda Street was the business premises.

The 1904 edition lists the same entry, but with a note that the business is "Koh Ah Kow & Co." I did not find this company name in the 1903 edition, so the firm may have been registered sometime in late 1903 or early 1904. I will check the Companies Registry files next week to confirm the registration date.

One interesting detail: the 1905 directory no longer lists Koh Ah Kow under merchants. Instead, there is a "Koh Ah Kow" under "General Dealers" with an address in Kreta Ayer Road. This could be the same person, but I cannot be certain without further evidence. I will note this as a possible lead, not a confirmed match.

---

**2024-05-30 (Thu)**
**Topic: Census returns – 1901**

Went to the National Archives this afternoon to look at the 1901 census returns for the Chinatown area. The returns are organised by street, and I was able to find the section for Pagoda Street.

Koh Ah Kow does not appear as a householder in the Pagoda Street section. The households listed for No. 5 Pagoda Street are mostly Chinese labourers and a few shopkeepers. None of the names match the Koh family I am tracing. This is consistent with my theory that Koh Ah Kow was not a resident of the property, but it does not rule out the possibility that he lived elsewhere in Chinatown.

I also checked the Kreta Ayer Road section, since the 1905 directory entry suggested a possible move. There is a Koh Ah Kow listed as a householder at 18 Kreta Ayer Road, with a household of five: himself, his wife, two sons, and one daughter. This is a promising lead, but I need to verify whether this is the same individual as the property dealer. The ages listed are: Koh Ah Kow, aged 42, occupation "dealer"; wife aged 38; sons aged 12 and 8; daughter aged 5. The occupation matches the 1905 directory entry, but I would need additional records to confirm the identity.

I will cross-reference this with the Chinese Protectorate records next. If the Protectorate files contain a business registration for Koh Ah Kow & Co., the address and the names of family members may help confirm the match.

---

**2024-06-03 (Mon)**
**Topic: Chinese Protectorate records – initial search**

The Chinese Protectorate records at the National Archives are not indexed by name, so I had to work through the registration files for 1903-1905 by date. I found a file for "Koh Ah Kow, merchant, 5 Pagoda Street" dated 1903-08-12. The file contains a business registration form and a photograph of the applicant.

The form lists the business as "Koh Ah Kow, General Merchant" and gives the address as 5 Pagoda Street. The applicant's age is given as 38, which would make him born around 1865. This is younger than the 42 recorded in the 1901 census, but the census ages are often approximate. The photograph may help me match the two records – I will bring a copy when I next visit the archives.

I also noted that the file contains a separate page with a stamp from the Registrar of Companies, dated 1904-02-03, indicating that the business was registered as "Koh Ah Kow & Co." on that date. This confirms the directory entry from 1904.

- Folio 112, Household No. 18: Koh Ah Chwee, head, age 53, occupation "carpenter." Tan Neo, wife, age 38. Children listed: Koh Cheng Kim, male, age 13; Koh Cheng Soon, male, age 8; Koh Cheng Huat, male, age 5; Koh Cheng Lian, female, age 2.
- The household composition matches the expected pattern. The address is recorded as 12 Upper Hokkien Street.
- Noted the age of Tan Neo as 38, which is consistent with a marriage in 1886 and a birth in 1888.
- Photocopy request submitted for Folio 112. Reference number PR-2024-0458.

---

**Monday, 17 June 2024 – FamilySearch Online Session (Home)**

Evening session, 7:30 pm – 9:00 pm.

- Searched the FamilySearch catalogue for the 1901 census index to cross-check the household details from NAS/REEL/001632.
- The index entry for Folio 112 matches the original return: Koh Ah Chwee, head, age 53; Tan Neo, wife, age 38; children Koh Cheng Kim, Koh Cheng Soon, Koh Cheng Huat, Koh Cheng Lian.
- Also searched for a possible death record for Koh Ah Chwee after 1901. No record found in the indexed death registers for 1901–1920 under "Koh Ah Chwee." Will check the burial records at the Christian cemetery and the undertaker's register in person.
- Saved the index page to /Koh_Family/Census_Records/1901.

---

**Thursday, 20 June 2024 – NAS Reading Room**

Morning session, 9:15 am – 12:00 pm.

- Requested NAS/REEL/001701 (Register of Births, Straits Settlements, Singapore, 1888–1890).
- Reel delivered at 9:30 am. The register is handwritten and the entries are arranged by quarter. I located the birth entry for Koh Cheng Kim, male, born 15 April 1888, at 12 Upper Hokkien Street. Father: Koh Ah Chwee, carpenter. Mother: Tan Neo.
- The entry confirms the birth date and parents' names. The 1891 census age of 2 and the 1901 census age of 13 both align with this birth date.
- Also searched the same register for a possible birth of a child between 1886 and 1888, in case there was an earlier child who did not survive. No Koh entry found in the 1886–1887 quarters.
- Photocopy request submitted for the birth entry. Reference number PR-2024-0463.

**Thursday, 27 June 2024 – NAS Reading Room**

Morning session, 9:20 am – 11:45 am.

- Requested NAS/REEL/001723 (Register of Deaths, Straits Settlements, Singapore, 1901–1905). Reel delivered at 9:40 am.
- The register is arranged by year and then by quarter. I searched all quarters for 1901–1905 for any entry under "Koh Ah Chwee" or variant spellings (Koh Ah Chui, Koh Ah Chwee, Koh Ah Chee).
- No matching entry found. This is consistent with the earlier absence in the indexed death registers. The family may have left Singapore, or the death may have occurred after 1905.
- Also searched the same reel for entries under "Tan Neo" for 1901–1905, in case a wife's death was recorded separately. No entry found.
- Photocopy request submitted for the index page of the 1901–1905 death register, showing the absence of entries. Reference number PR-2024-0471.

---

**Friday, 28 June 2024 – Christian Cemetery Office**

Afternoon session, 2:00 pm – 4:30 pm.

- Visited the office of the Christian cemetery at Bukit Brown Road. The purpose was to check the burial registers for any record of Koh Ah Chwee or Tan Neo between 1901 and 1920.
- The office holds registers for the old Christian cemetery (Fort Canning) and the newer municipal cemetery. The staff member on duty, Mr. Lim, was helpful and brought out the Fort Canning burial register for 1900–1910.
- No entry for Koh Ah Chwee or Tan Neo in the 1900–1910 register. Mr. Lim noted that the Fort Canning register for 1911–1920 is held at the NAS annexe, not at the office. He suggested checking the undertaker's register, which is also at the annexe.
- The undertaker's register for 1900–1920 is a separate series. Mr. Lim said it is not indexed by name and would require a page-by-page search. I decided to defer this to a future session, as the time needed is uncertain.
- No photocopy request was submitted from this visit. The office does not provide photocopying; they only allow manual transcription.

---

**Saturday, 29 June 2024 – FamilySearch Online Session (Home)**

Morning session, 9:00 am – 10:30 am.

- Searched the FamilySearch catalogue for the undertaker's register for Singapore, 1900–1920. The register is not digitised; it is listed as available on microfilm only.
- The microfilm number is given as FS/REEL/002114. This matches the series I saw at the cemetery office. I will request this reel at the NAS annexe on the next visit.
- Also searched for any probate records for Koh Ah Chwee. The indexed probate records for the Straits Settlements cover 1827–1930. No entry found under "Koh Ah Chwee" or "Koh Ah Chui."
- Saved the search results page to /Koh_Family/Cemetery_Records.

---

**Monday, 1 July 2024 – NAS Annexe, Cemetery Records Section**

Morning session, 9:30 am – 12:15 pm.

- Requested FS/REEL/002114 (Undertaker's Register, Singapore, 1900–1920). Reel delivered at 9:45 am.
- The register is handwritten and entries are arranged chronologically by date of burial. Each entry gives the name, age, cause of death, place of residence, and the name of the person who arranged the burial.
- I searched the register page by page for the period 1901–1920. The handwriting is variable and some entries are faded. I found no entry for Koh Ah Chwee or Tan Neo.
- The register does include several entries for persons named Koh, but none with the given name Ah Chwee or with a wife named Tan Neo. The ages and addresses of the Koh entries do not match the family profile.
- Noted the absence in the log. The death record for Koh Ah Chwee remains unlocated. Possible next steps: (1) check the 1911 census for the household, in case the family moved; (2) check the emigration lists for departures to China; (3) check the land records for 12 Upper Hokkien Street after 1901.
- Photocopy request submitted for two pages of the undertaker's register, showing the absence of matching entries. Reference number PR-2024-0478.

**Archival Research Log – Koh Family Tree Project**

---

**Wednesday, 3 July 2024 – NAS Annexe, Land Records Section**

Morning session, 9:15 am – 12:30 pm.

- Requested the land records series for Upper Hokkien Street, 1890–1910. The series is filed by street name and then by lot number. The archivist on duty, Mr. Goh, helped me locate the file for 12 Upper Hokkien Street.
- The file contains the original Crown lease, dated 1889, and a series of transfer documents. The original lessee is recorded as Tan Kim Seng, who leased the lot for a term of 99 years. The lease was transferred to Koh Ah Chwee in 1895.
- The transfer document, dated 12 March 1895, is a printed form with handwritten insertions. It records the sale price as $1,200 Straits dollars. The witnesses are two men named Lim Boon Keng and Chia Cheng Hoe. The document is signed with a thumbprint by Koh Ah Chwee, which is consistent with the family story that he could not write in English.
- There is a further transfer document in the file, dated 1903, transferring the lease from Koh Ah Chwee to a man named Lee Chin Tian. This is the first record I have found that shows the family left the property before 1911.
- No document in the file mentions a wife or children of Koh Ah Chwee. The land records are silent on family members.
- Photocopy request submitted for the 1895 transfer document and the 1903 transfer document. Reference number PR-2024-0481.

---

**Saturday, 6 July 2024 – FamilySearch Online Session (Home)**

Morning session, 9:00 am – 11:00 am.

- Searched the 1911 Straits Settlements census for the household. The census is indexed and searchable by name. I searched for "Koh Ah Chwee" and "Tan Neo" with no results.
- I then searched by address, using the enumeration district for Upper Hokkien Street. The 1911 census does not show any household at 12 Upper Hokkien Street. This is consistent with the 1903 transfer of the lease.
- I also searched for the names of the children known from the family tree: Koh Beng Hean, Koh Beng Huat, and Koh Beng Kim. No entries were found in the 1911 census index.
- The absence of the family from the 1911 census suggests they may have left Singapore before the census was taken. The next step is to check the emigration lists for departures to China.
- Saved the census search results page to /Koh_Family/Census_Records.

---

**Monday, 8 July 2024 – NAS Annexe, Emigration Records Section**

Morning session, 10:00 am – 12:45 pm.

- Requested the emigration lists for departures to China, 1900–1910. The lists are arranged by ship and then by date of departure. The archivist warned me that the lists for this period are incomplete; some ships' lists have not survived.
- I searched the lists for the period 1903–1908, which is the most likely window for the family's departure. The lists are handwritten and the names are recorded in both Chinese characters and romanised form where the passenger gave a romanised name.
- I found no entry for Koh Ah Chwee, Tan Neo, or any of the three children in the surviving lists.
- I noted that the lists for 1905 and 1906 are missing from the series. If the family departed in either of those years, their names would not appear in the surviving records.
- The absence of the family from the emigration lists is inconclusive. The family may have left on a ship whose list has not survived, or they may have travelled on a private vessel not recorded in the lists.
- Photocopy request submitted for the index page of the emigration lists, showing the missing years. Reference number PR-2024-0490.
